Same-rank placement provides no substantive developmental direction evidence, so a symmetric coherence relation is the supported judgment rather than buildsTowards. Shared LC tags/text ('equation', 'unknown') corroborate the same skill family rather than mere wording overlap. judgment.rationale: Both Indicators sit under the same BASIC 4 Content Standard B4.2.2.2 ("Solve one-step equations involving a symbol to represent an unknown number") in Strand 2: Algebra, Sub-strand 2: Unknowns, Expressions and Equations, and both are at coordinate rank 0 (BASIC 4), so direction rests on statement content rather than grade. Proficiency in interpreting the equation therefore supports success in the trial-and-verify solution strategy, supporting second_to_first; the reverse (solving procedurally supporting oral interpretation) is less directly supported by the texts. Shared wording alone ("given", "one-step", "equation") was not treated as sufficient; the judgment rests on the interpret-then-solve content distinction. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators (same rank 0) under the same Content Standard B4.1.1.1 (quantities and place value for multi-digit whole numerals) in Strand Number / Sub-strand Counting, Representation & Cardinality, so hierarchy and rank alone do not settle the judgment. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same rank) under the same Measurement Content Standard 'Demonstrate an understanding of volume of common 3D shapes'. B5.3.3.2.2 has learners determine the volume of boxes by counting how many 1cm³ cubes fit inside, establishing volume as an accumulation of cubic-centimetre units. B5.3.3.2.4 extends that unit-based conception outward: its Learning Components require describing the relationship between capacity and volume and between litre and 10cm3, which presupposes that volume is already understood as a count of cubic units. Proficiency with cubic-unit volume measurement therefore substantively supports success in relating capacity/litre to cubic measure, justifying a same-rank developmental direction beyond mere shared parent, shared 'volume' token, or code/page proximity.

The remaining nomination signals (shared ancestors, shared tag 'area', stop-word token/trigram overlap, weak code prefix, weak page proximity) are explicitly weak or generic and cannot by themselves license buildsTowards in either direction. Canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the supported judgment; endpoint order is technical only. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain items at the same resolved coordinate (Grade BASIC 5, rank 1) under the same Algebra / Patterns and Relationships Content Standard B5.2.1.1 ('Determine the pattern rule to make predictions about subsequent elements'), so the grain and topic match and same-rank direction must rest on statement substance rather than shared ancestry, code prefix, or page proximity. The first Indicator (B5.2.1.1.4) asks learners to represent a given pattern visually to verify predictions (LC tags: pattern, predictions, visual representation); the second (B5.2.1.1.7) asks learners to write a rule in words and in algebra to represent a given pattern, decomposed into LCs for a verbal rule and an algebraic rule. Constructing and checking a visual representation of a pattern establishes the structure and verified regularity that a learner must articulate to state that regularity as a generalized verbal and symbolic rule; the second is the more abstract symbolic generalization of the same pattern work, so proficiency in the visual/verification indicator supports success in the rule-writing indicator. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), limiting exemplar-level detail.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 4 Indicators (rank 0, same grade coordinate) in Strand 1 NUMBER, Sub-strand 3: Fractions, so any developmental direction would need substantive same-rank evidence. B4.1.3.2.1 concerns comparing and ordering like-denominator fractions via pictorial representations and equivalent fractions with the LCD (LCs: compare/order fractions, LCD, pictorial), while B4.1.3.1.4 concerns recognising, drawing and labelling improper fractions (LCs: recognise/draw/label improper fractions). These are complementary Basic 4 fraction-representation skills that reinforce one another (pictorial modelling and symbolic labelling of fractions), but neither statement's proficiency is shown by the bounded evidence to be a substantive enabler of the other: improper-fraction recognition is not required to compare like-denominator fractions, and comparing/ordering does not extend into improper-fraction notation. Source code prefix, page proximity and the single shared token 'fractions' are weak nomination signals only, and the parent Content Standards carry a known Basic 4 Fractions editorial code anomaly (B4.1.3.1/B4.1.3.2 merge context), which further weakens any code-order-based directional inference. Symmetric conceptual coherence is supported; dependency is not.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Indicators (rank 2) under the same Content Standard B6.1.2.6 'Demonstrate an understanding of integers' (Strand 1: Number, Sub-Strand 2: Number Operations), so grain and scope match. Second (B6.1.2.6.2) is additive integer work — 'Solve simple addition and subtraction problems involving integers (excluding subtraction of negative numbers)', with LCs for simple addition and simple subtraction of integers; first (B6.1.1.4.3) is 'Perform simple multiplication with integers' (LC tags: integers, multiplication, operations). Since integer multiplication extends signed-number combination beyond additive operations (repeated addition / sign rules on the number line), proficiency with simple integer addition and subtraction supports success with simple integer multiplication, giving a same-rank second_to_first developmental direction; the bounded source table also places the additive indicator at row 8 and the multiplication indicator at row 9 within the same window, consistent with that order rather than the reverse. Evidence limits: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the multiplication indicator's code B6.1.1.4.3 does not share the prefix of its parent standard B6.1.2.6, a code anomaly that was not used as positive hierarchy evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators (same coordinate rank 0) sharing parent Content Standard B4.4.1.1 ('many-to-one correspondence in displaying, and reading or interpreting, graphs') in Strand 4: Data. B4.4.1.1.4 asks learners to find real-world print/electronic media graphs using many-to-one correspondence and describe that correspondence; B4.4.1.1.3 asks learners to compare graphs displaying the same data and explain similarities and differences. Their Learning Components ('describe the many-to-one correspondence used in graphs' vs 'compare graphs in which the same data has been displayed' / 'explain how graphs displaying the same data are the same and different') show substantive coherence in graph reading and interpretation, but neither skill is evidenced as prerequisite to the other: locating and describing correspondence in media graphs and comparing alternative displays of one data set are complementary interpretive tasks. Same-rank placement and adjacent codes/pages provide no developmental direction, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are Indicator-grain siblings (B4.1.1.4.1 and B4.1.1.4.2) under the same Content Standard 'Interpret negative and positive numbers in context', Sub-Strand 'Counting, Representation & Cardinality', at the same resolved coordinate BASIC 4 (rank 0). Their statement texts and LCs show substantive conceptual coherence about positive/negative values: one asks learners to describe real-life situations using positive and negative values (contextual interpretation), the other to count forwards and backwards with positive and negative whole numbers through zero (ordered number-line/counting skill). These are complementary facets of the same integer-concept standard rather than one clearly enabling the other: contextual description does not presuppose counting through zero, and counting through zero does not presuppose real-life interpretation. Same-rank developmental direction would need substantive evidence beyond code sequence and shared table row/page, which the bounded evidence (weak local-rank, code-prefix, and page-proximity signals; modest token/trigram overlap on 'positive'/'negative') does not supply. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment. Both endpoints and all ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, and source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), limiting exemplar-level detail.

These are substantively coherent, mutually reinforcing facets of perimeter work in the same units and the same instructional standard: estimation builds magnitude sense for boundary length, while construction explores the inverse, non-unique relationship between perimeter and shape. Developmental dependency is not supported: the two indicators are at the same BASIC 4 rank, and estimation with length referents is not a skill whose proficiency materially supports success at the additive/spatial reasoning of generating several rectangles with a fixed perimeter; the remaining nomination signals (shared parent/ancestors, B4.3.3.1 code prefix, 'perimeter' LC tag and token/trigram overlap, weak rank_gap-0 proximity) cannot by themselves license buildsTowards in either direction. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (rank 1) under the same Algebra / Patterns and Relationships Content Standard B5.2.1.1 'Determine the pattern rule to make predictions about subsequent elements'. B5.2.1.1.2 asks learners to describe a given pattern orally or in writing using mathematical language (one more, one less, five more, one more/less than twice), i.e. articulating the structure of a pattern; B5.2.1.1.5 asks learners to solve a given problem by using a pattern rule to determine subsequent elements, i.e. applying an articulated rule to extend a pattern in a problem context. The verbal/written characterisation of a pattern is the substantive basis for stating and applying a pattern rule, so proficiency in the descriptive indicator supports success in the problem-solving indicator; the added complexity (rule application and prediction within a problem) justifies the same-rank developmental direction from the second SFI to the first. Endpoint and ancestor audit/merge context plus truncated source evidence were considered and do not contradict this reading, though only bounded excerpts were available.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 6 Indicators (same statement-type grain, identical coordinate rank 2, no developmental gap). B6.2.3.1.2 (Strand 2 Algebra, Sub-Strand Variables and Equations, under B6.2.3.1 on single-variable one-step equations) requires identifying the unknown, representing a problem with an equation, and solving it concretely, pictorially or symbolically; B6.1.2.5.1 (Strand 1 Number, Sub-Strand Number Operations, under B6.1.2.5 'Translate word problems into mathematical sentences and solve') requires solving multi-step word problems involving the four basic operations. There is genuine conceptual coherence: both translate word-problem situations into mathematical sentences/equations and solve them, and the algebraic equation-representation work complements number-operation multi-step problem solving. However, the evidence shows no substantive same-rank dependency — the algebra indicator is scoped to one-step single-variable equations while the number indicator is scoped to multi-step four-operation computation, so neither can be shown to be the proficiency base for the other; token/trigram and code-prefix overlap are weak ('solve', 'the', shared 'b6' segment) and the shared Grade ancestor alone is not semantic evidence. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted evidence items each), so scope detail beyond the bounded excerpts is unverified.

judgment.rationale: Both Indicators sit in BASIC 4, Strand 1 NUMBER, Sub-strand 3 Fractions (rank 0 for both), so direction rests on statement substance rather than coordinate gap. B4.1.3.1.1 (second) has learners generate unit fractions and locate a unit fraction on a number line by partitioning 0-1 into equal parts, with LCs 'Generate unit fractions' and 'Locate a unit fraction on a number line ... partitioning it into equal parts'; this establishes part-whole meaning and fraction magnitude. Note the Basic 4 Fractions code anomaly in the parent Content Standards (B4.1.3.1 kept separate, B4.1.3.2 merged from a mislabelled row); this affects code interpretation only, not the substantive skill relation, and the two SFIs' own source excerpts are complete and non-conflicting despite truncated source-evidence lists.

judgment.rationale: Both are Basic 4 (rank 0) Indicators under the same merged Content Standard B4.1.3.2 in Sub-strand 3: Fractions (Strand 1: Number), so the grain and topic match. B4.1.3.2.3 'Provide examples of where fractions are used' develops contextual/application awareness of fractions, while B4.1.3.1.3 'Find the simplest form of given fractions by dividing through by the highest common factor' is a distinct procedural competence (HCF cancelling). Their coherence is complementary reinforcement of fraction understanding within one content standard, which supports symmetric relatesTo rather than buildsTowards. Note the parent Content Standard carries a documented B4.1.3.1/B4.1.3.2 mislabelling merge, so source code prefixes were not used as positive evidence, and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each).

Direction is not asserted from code ordering or shared ancestry alone. Evidence limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each), and the parent B5.3.2.2 carries a same_code_different_content audit flag plus merged Sub-Strand/Grade organizers, so hierarchy context must be read with that audit context in mind.

B6.1.1.1.3 concerns locating numbers in positions around a given number on a number chart (number-sequence and relative-position sense); B6.1.1.1.5 concerns rounding whole numbers up to 100,000 to nearest ten thousands/thousands/hundreds/tens, whose LCs tag place value and round off/up/down. Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment; token overlap ('numbers', code prefix) alone was not treated as evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Indicators (same grade rank 2) in Strand 1: Number, Sub-Strand 4: Ratios and Proportion, so the statement-type grain matches. The first (B6.1.4.1.1) establishes the ratio concept itself via concrete models and pictorial representations, plus symbolic writing and simplest form (LCs: 'use concrete models... to explain a ratio', 'write a ratio symbolically', 'write a ratio in its simplest form'). Despite equal grade rank, the substantive evidence is directional: proficiency in representing and simplifying ratios supports success in reasoning about proportion as equal ratios, so first_to_second is justified rather than symmetric relatesTo. Shared modeling language and code prefix alone were not treated as sufficient.

B5.1.3.1.1 ('Determine equivalent fractions of given fractions') and B5.1.3.1.6 ('Use models to explain the result of multiplying a fraction by whole number') are substantively coherent complementary fraction-sense skills within the same BASIC 5 fraction-operations programme: equivalence/renaming and model-based interpretation of fraction multiplication mutually reinforce understanding of fractional quantity. This is more than word or code overlap, so canonical relatesTo is warranted. buildsTowards is not chosen: the endpoints share the same rank, and the only supplied signals are shared ancestry, a weak shared code prefix (B5.1.3.1), weak rank proximity (gap 0) and trivial token/trigram overlap ('of', fraction substrings); no bounded excerpt shows that determining equivalent fractions is required by, or measurably enables, modelling multiplication of a fraction by a whole number (that skill rests chiefly on unit-fraction/repeated-addition reasoning). Exemplar evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each), so a developmental claim would rest on reconstructed content; confidence is moderate for the same reason. All endpoint, ancestor and request-wide audit/merge/code-context and truncation warnings are retained.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Indicators (rank 2) under Strand 4: Data, Sub-strand 1 (Data Collection, Organization, Presentation, Interpretation and Analysis), so the judgment stays within one statement-type grain. B6.4.1.1.3 (second) has learners draw a line graph from a supplied table of values and answer questions on it to interpret and draw conclusions; its LCs are 'Draw a line graph for a given table of values' and 'Answer questions based on a line graph to interpret it and draw conclusions'. B6.4.1.2.3 (first) requires designing and administering a questionnaire, recording the data, then 'analyse and graph the results to solve problems' (LCs include 'Graph the results of collected data to solve problems' and 'Analyse the results of collected data to solve problems'). Graphing and interpreting data that is already organised in a table is the narrower enabling competence that supports the broader, self-generated data-collection investigation, which extends the same graphing/interpretation work to learner-collected data and problem solving; same-rank direction is therefore supported by this substantive difference in scope rather than by shared ancestry, code prefix, or generic token overlap (shared tokens are largely function words plus 'graph'/'data'). Confidence is moderate because the two indicators sit under different Content Standards (B6.4.1.1 line graphs vs B6.4.1.2 data-collection methods) and the questionnaire indicator does not specify the graph type.

The nomination rests on shared parent ancestors, weak code-prefix overlap (b6.1.1), same-grade rank proximity (gap 0, no substantive developmental evidence), and generic token/trigram overlap of 'numbers', 'up', 'to', '100' — surface features the policy says cannot establish a relation. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators in Strand 2: Algebra (same statement-type grain, identical coordinate rank 0), but they sit under different Sub-Strands and Content Standards: B4.2.1.3.1 'Translate the information in a given problem into a table or chart' under 'Patterns and Relationships' / B4.2.1.3 (represent and extend patterns using charts and tables), while B4.2.2.2.5 'Identify the unknown in a problem, represent the problem with an equation, and solve the problem concretely, pictorially or symbolically' sits under 'Unknowns, Expressions and Equations' / B4.2.2.2 (one-step equations). They share substantive coherence as complementary mathematising skills — extracting information from a word problem and rendering it in a mathematical representation (table/chart vs. equation) to support solution — evidenced by the LC set ('Translate the information in a given problem into a table or chart' vs. 'Identify the unknown in a problem', 'Represent the problem with an equation'). However, neither statement extends, deepens, or presupposes the other: table/chart translation for pattern work and equation formulation for unknowns are parallel representational strands at the same grade rank, and the nomination signals (shared 'problem'/stopword tokens, shared Strand/Grade ancestors, weak 'b4.2' code prefix) do not supply the substantive same-rank evidence required for a developmental direction. Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.

LC tags corroborate the shared 'factors'/'numbers' skill core ('factors, numbers, sets' vs 'factors, representation, square numbers'). Same-rank direction rests on this substantive skill dependency, not on code order or shared parentage alone. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so exemplar detail is unavailable, but the statement texts are unambiguous.

Shared LC tokens ('pattern', 'explain', 'element') reflect this genuine conceptual continuity rather than generic wording alone; source-code prefix and rank proximity were treated only as nomination signals. judgment.rationale: Both are same-grain Indicators (BASIC 6, rank 2) under the same Content Standard B6.2.1.1 'Determine the pattern rule to make predictions about subsequent elements' in Algebra / Pattern and Relationships, so shared placement alone is not decisive. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 6 Indicators (same statement grain, same canonical Grade rank 2) in Strand 4: Data, Sub-strand 1 (Data Collection, Organization, Presentation, Interpretation and Analysis), under different Content Standards: B6.4.1.1 (create, label and interpret line graphs) and B6.4.1.2 (select, justify and use appropriate methods of collecting data). B6.4.1.1.2 is a representational judgement — decide whether a data set suits a line graph (continuous) or a series of points (discrete) and explain why — with LCs on data representation and reasoned justification. B6.4.1.2.3 is a questionnaire investigation — design, administer, record, analyse and graph results to solve problems. The two are substantively coherent: choosing and justifying how data should be displayed sits alongside collecting, analysing and graphing one's own data, so they mutually reinforce the sub-strand's data-handling cycle beyond mere shared ancestry, the weak 'b6/4/1' code prefix, or 'data'/'graph' token overlap. But no developmental dependency is evidenced at equal rank: B6.4.1.2.3's graphing and analysis LCs are generic and never invoke the continuous/discrete distinction, the two indicators sit under sibling Content Standards with no stated ordering, and the rank-proximity signal is explicitly weak with rank_gap 0. Canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the correct complete judgment. Evidence limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, including the merged case-variant BASIC 6 Grade organizer; these remain unresolved.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators of the same grain under Content Standard B4.1.1.3 ('Demonstrate an understanding of factors, multiples and squared numbers'), Sub-Strand Counting, Representation & Cardinality, Strand NUMBER, at the same resolved BASIC 4 coordinate (rank 0). Beyond shared placement, the statement texts and Learning Components show a pair-specific progression: B4.1.1.3.1 asks learners to generate the complete set of factors of a single given number up to 50 (systematic divisibility listing for one number), whereas B4.1.1.3.3 requires determining the lowest common multiple of at least two given numbers up to 100 — a larger number range, two or more numbers at once, and comparison/selection across generated lists. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Indicators in Strand 1: Number (rank 2, same grade), but their substance diverges. B6.1.1.1.3 (Sub-Strand 1: Counting, Representation, Cardinality & Ordinality, under B6.1.1.1 on quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals up to 1 billion) requires locating numbers in positions around a given number on a number chart, with LC tags 'identify', 'number chart', 'position'. The nomination rests only on shared Grade/Strand ancestry, zero-gap same-rank proximity, a weak 'b6.1' code prefix, and negligible lexical overlap (jaccard 0.045, shared token 'a'; trigrams 'ent','ion','ons','tio'), which alone never establish a relation. There is no evidence that whole-number chart position identification supports fraction comparison/ordering proficiency or vice versa, and no substantive conceptual coherence beyond the generic 'number' domain, so neither a permitted buildsTowards direction nor relatesTo is supported. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, but the available statement text and LCs are consistent and unambiguous, so this is a settled negative rather than ambiguity.

The shared tokens ('lowest','common') are not the basis of the judgment; the LCM-to-LCD skill dependency is. These are complementary stages of one coherent data-handling process, giving substantive conceptual coherence, but neither statement's proficiency is evidenced as supporting success in the other: drawing a line graph from a supplied table does not depend on having chosen a collection method, and vice versa. Same-rank placement with no substantive developmental evidence, and the nomination's lexical signals ('a', 'for', 'given', 'the') plus the weak shared code prefix are generic and carry no developmental weight, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each); the bounded excerpts were nevertheless sufficient for this reading.

Recorded as symmetric relatesTo. Nomination signals are weak and non-semantic: shared Grade/Strand ancestors, weak local-rank proximity (gap 0), a weak 'b6.1' code prefix, and token/trigram overlap limited to stopwords ('and', 'to'). Reading and writing large numerals does not specifically support proportional-reasoning strategies with rates and scales, and there is no substantive shared concept or representation beyond generic numeracy, so neither a developmental direction nor meaningful conceptual coherence is supported.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators under Strand 1 NUMBER, Sub-strand 1 (Counting, Representation & Cardinality), but their substantive content differs materially. Neither statement's proficiency demonstrably supports the other: base-ten place-value modelling is not a stated or implied support for contextual interpretation of directed numbers, and integer contexts do not extend the place-value modelling work here. The nomination rests on shared ancestry, a weak code prefix (b4.1.1), same-grade rank proximity, and a single shared token 'using' (Jaccard ~0.04), which per policy do not by themselves establish either relation. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), so absence of a closer link cannot be proved, but the trustworthy available text supports no dependency or substantive skill coherence.

B6.2.1.1.4 asks learners to represent a given pattern visually to verify predictions; B6.2.1.1.8 asks learners to describe the relationship in a given table or chart using a mathematical expression. These are complementary representational treatments of the same pattern-rule content (pictorial verification alongside tabular/symbolic description), which is substantive, pair-specific instructional coherence rather than mere shared parentage or word overlap. However, the evidence does not establish a developmental dependency in either direction at the same rank: the only ordering signal is the sibling code sequence (.4 before .8), which is not semantic, and the source table context shows B6.2.1.1.8 following B6.2.1.1.7 (writing a rule in words and algebra), not the visual-verification indicator. Same-rank buildsTowards therefore lacks the required substantive support, so the symmetric relatesTo judgment is recorded with null direction and canonical endpoint order preserved. Material limitation: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge/code context, so exemplar-level detail that might evidence a dependency is unavailable and confidence is moderate.

producer_judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators (same rank 0) in Strand 3 Geometry and Measurement, Sub-strand 3 Measurement- (Perimeter and Area), but under different Content Standards: B4.3.3.1 (perimeter of regular/irregular shapes) and B4.3.3.2 (area of regular/irregular 2-D shapes). Source-code ordering (B4.3.3.1.2 before B4.3.3.2.1) is not treated as positive developmental evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same statement-type grain, same rank 1, no forward grade gap) under Strand 1 Number / Sub-strand 1 Counting, Representation & Cardinality, but under different Content Standards: B5.1.1.2.1 'Recognize Roman Numerals system up to C (i.e. 100)' (parent B5.1.1.2, Roman numerals) and B5.1.1.1.1 'Model number quantities up to 1,000,000 using graph sheets and multi-base block' (parent B5.1.1.1, quantities and place value). The substantive coherence is that both develop representation of number quantities with a symbol/representation system, so the place-value modelling work and the Roman-numeral symbol work reinforce each other as complementary representations of number within the same sub-strand. Neither statement is a deepening, extension, or enabling condition of the other: Roman numerals are non-positional and capped at 100, while the modelling indicator concerns positional place value to 1,000,000, so no directional buildsTowards is warranted; the shared-ancestor, weak code-prefix, and trivial token overlap ('to','up') evidence adds no developmental signal. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Content Standards (same grain, same canonical rank 0) under Strand 3 Geometry and Measurement, but in different sub-strands: '2D and 3D Shapes' (B4.3.1.1, identify lines of symmetry of regular and irregular 2D shapes) and 'Measurement- (Perimeter and Area)' (B4.3.3.1, demonstrate understanding of perimeter of regular and irregular shapes). They share the same substantive objects of study - regular and irregular 2D shapes and attention to their sides/properties - so they are complementary shape-analysis work that reinforces one another, but neither attribute (symmetry vs. perimeter/length estimation and summation of side lengths) is required for the other, and equal grade rank with no substantive sequencing evidence does not support a developmental direction. Shared code prefix (b4.3), token/trigram overlap driven mainly by the phrase 'regular and irregular shapes', and the common Strand/Grade ancestors are nomination signals only, so only the symmetric relation is asserted. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (26 and 28 omitted items), limiting confirmation of any deeper linkage; the B4.3.3.1 endpoint also carries a merge note about a known same-code collision with a distinct Position/Transformation occurrence, which does not affect the perimeter content used here.

The two statements address disjoint content: symbolic equation solving versus spatial transformation of plane figures, with no shared representation, procedure, or dependency evident in the bounded text. The nomination rests only on the shared BASIC 6 grade ancestor (rank 2 for both, gap 0), weak 'b6' code-prefix overlap, and incidental lexical overlap on the word 'single' and trigrams such as 'sin'/'gle'/'tio' — none of which is pair-specific instructional coherence. Neither endpoint supplies Learning Components to support a finer link, and both have truncated source evidence, but the visible statements are clear enough that neither a permitted developmental direction nor substantive conceptual coherence is supported. Note also that the second endpoint carries a same_code_different_content audit flag for code B6.3.3.5; this does not alter the judgment since the transformation description is the one used here.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 4 Content Standards (same grain, same rank 0), but they sit in different strands with distinct content: B4.1.1.1 concerns quantities and place value for multi-digit whole numerals to 100,000 (Number / Counting, Representation & Cardinality), while B4.2.2.2 concerns solving one-step equations with a symbol representing an unknown (Algebra / Unknowns, Expressions and Equations). The nomination rests on a shared Grade ancestor, same-rank proximity, a shared 'b4' code segment, and trivial token/trigram overlap ('an', 'to', 'num', 'qua'), none of which is pair-specific semantic evidence. Place-value/magnitude understanding of large numerals is not a substantive support for solving one-step symbol equations (which draw on addition/subtraction operation sense), and no supplied text, Learning Components (none present for either), or hierarchy evidence links them instructionally. Source evidence for both SFIs is truncated, but the visible statements are unambiguous, so the judgment is a negative rather than unresolved.

Incidental mention of the distributive property does not create pattern-generalisation coherence, and neither statement's proficiency is shown to support the other.

Despite equal grade rank, the substantive pair-specific evidence supports a forward direction: multi-digit division procedures (as evidenced in the source row 'Divide 3-digit numbers by 1-digit number efficiently') depend on fluent multi-digit multiplication for estimating quotients, forming partial products, and checking results, so proficiency in the multiplication standard supports success in the division standard. The shared code prefix, token/trigram overlap, and shared ancestors alone were not treated as sufficient; the operational dependency between multiplication and division of multi-digit numbers is the basis. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge/code context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted source-evidence items each), so the judgment rests only on the bounded statement text and hierarchy shown.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same statement-type grain, same canonical rank 1) sharing parent Content Standard B5.1.4.1 on decimal fractions. B5.1.4.1.5 asks learners to use models to explain the result of multiplying a decimal (up to the thousandths) by a whole number; B5.1.4.1.2 asks them to compare and order decimal fractions and mixtures of common and decimal fractions (up to the thousandths) with <, >, =. They share the same decimal place-value domain to thousandths and are mutually reinforcing (magnitude/ordering reasoning alongside modelled multiplication), giving substantive conceptual coherence. However, the evidence shows coordinate skills within one standard rather than a dependency: comparison/ordering is relational reasoning while the other is operational modelling, and with equal grade rank and no Learning Components the sibling code sequence (.2 before .5) is only source ordering and cannot establish a developmental direction. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment.

With equal rank, no substantive evidence justifies a developmental direction, so the symmetric relation is chosen. B5.1.2.1.2 asks learners to apply mental multiplication strategies (annexing then adding zeros, halving and doubling, use of the distributive property) under a content standard on mental mathematics strategies and basic multiplication facts to 81.
